sections.html:
Tax work stays in Morganfield, where the PVA and the sheriff share the 100 West Main Street address. The PVA is a state office with county jurisdiction, charged with valuing property as of January 1. Rates, the arithmetic and the collecting all belong to others.

  • PVA: PO Box 177, Morganfield, KY 42437. Call (270) 389-1933 between 8:00 and 4:00 on weekdays. Exemption forms go here.
  • Sheriff, the payee: PO Box 30, Morganfield, KY 42437. Phone (270) 389-1303, with the same weekday hours.
  • County Clerk, who records deeds and later holds unpaid bills: (270) 389-1334.

The county government site adds a tax roll search, a tax calculator and a rate page under the PVA menu, handy for checking a parcel before you call.

Union occupies the northwest tip of Kentucky, looking over the Ohio River. Four cities share the county: Morganfield, the seat and largest, plus Sturgis, Uniontown and Waverly. US 60, KY 56 and KY 109 carry the traffic. Union County Public Schools runs schools in the same three towns that have library branches.

The county has been losing people for decades: 13,668 in the 2020 count and an estimate of 12,839 for July 2025.

sections.h2: The state rate and the homestead deduction
sections.html:
Frankfort's real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents on each hundred dollars of assessed value, lower than the 10.9 cents charged in 2024. County, school and other districts bring the full bill well above it.

The $49,100 homestead deduction lowers the taxable base on a qualifying house. About 21.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, and 23.1 percent of those younger than 65 live with a disability, so many households may be eligible. Apply at the PVA on West Main. A disability based claim needs yearly renewal. Owners with service connected disabilities and owners deemed permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems do not have to renew.

KRS 134.015 sets one schedule for all counties. Union's sheriff takes 2 percent off before November 2, bills the face amount until the year ends, charges 5 percent for January and 10 percent once February arrives, and tacks on a sheriff's fee.

On April 15 the sheriff gives the County Clerk its list of overdue bills and a lien goes on each parcel. The sale of those bills normally falls in September, a year after the tax year, with the date put on the website roughly a month earlier. Anyone who wants to bid registers with the clerk first, and the state also requires registration for a buyer taking more than three certificates in this county, more than five statewide, or putting in more than $10,000.

sections.h2: What a late bill grows into
sections.html:
A late bill grows in steps. A 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's add on and a commission lift it by the time the clerk receives it. Interest of 1 percent a month then runs, and commissions follow the interest. Each notice the attorney sends adds cost, and the figure is higher again once the newspaper notice runs. An investor who buys at the sale then adds charges of their own.

Under KRS 134.420 the lien can last eleven years, and a new owner inherits it along with the land. If you owe back taxes, ask the clerk for a payoff number and let the title company send it at closing.

Meet with the PVA before filing anything, since the state refuses appeals that skip that conversation. Each May the roll is displayed for thirteen days, beginning with the first Monday. After the meeting, hand the appeal to the clerk before the next day ends once display closes.

Local owners acting as the board of assessment appeals convene 25 to 35 days later, for as many as five days. It denies an appeal that lacks factual support, so collect sale comparisons, repair bids and photos. An owner who neither files nor shows up cannot go further to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Any change comes with a written reason, audio recording is allowed, and a higher final figure means an extra bill.

sections.h2: Deeds and records at the County Clerk
sections.html:
The clerk's office at 100 West Main Street holds recorded land documents going back to 1811, mostly deeds, mortgages, assignments and releases. A deed is lodged where the land lies and must cite how the seller got title (KRS 382.110). KRS 382.135 adds the parties' mailing addresses, the full price, an in care of address for that year's bill and a sworn price certificate.

The clerk offers e-filing so a title company can send documents without mail or courier. Residents searching for personal reasons can use the online index free, five searches a day, and the same books can be viewed in the office at no cost. Commercial researchers pay $65 a month per county through the records vendor.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or a house that needs work
sections.html:
An owner with a tenant, a probate delay or a house needing work can sell as is for cash instead of waiting for a retail buyer's inspection. Taxes owed do not block that sale. Get the sheriff's figure for the current year and the clerk's figure for anything older, then give both to the closing agent.

Check the clerk's records to confirm the deed matches the name on the sale contract. Ask the PVA whether your exemption is on file. And compare any offer by what you would keep after payoffs, not by price alone. A buyer who pays cash can often close on a date you pick.

Before you meet a buyer, put together a short folder: the latest tax bill, the deed, any exemption paperwork and a payoff letter if there is a mortgage. Bring a photo ID to the courthouse when you ask for written figures, and ask each office to date them. Penalties and interest change the totals, so a figure from close to closing day is the one that counts. If the house came through an estate, add the papers that show who may sign.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Union County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Bring it to the sheriff at 100 West Main Street, Morganfield, or mail it to PO Box 30. Questions go to (270) 389-1303 during weekday hours, 8:00 to 4:00.

faqs.q: Does the Union County PVA send my bill?
faqs.a: No. The PVA only values property and handles exemptions, and it leaves rates, tax calculation and collection to others. The sheriff handles billing and payment.

faqs.q: When is the Union County delinquent tax sale?
faqs.a: September, in the year after the tax year, is the usual month. The County Clerk posts the exact date on the county website about a month ahead, at (270) 389-1334 for questions.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Union County parcel online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county government site has a tax roll search and a tax calculator under the PVA pages, plus a rate page, so you can see the owner and assessed value.

faqs.q: How much is a house worth in Union County?
faqs.a: The midpoint for 2020 to 2024 is $104,500. Median rent is $790, and owners live in 70.2 percent of homes.
